html:
The Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in Bombay in 1875 by the monk Dayananda Saraswati. Its call was a return to the Vedas, the oldest Hindu scriptures, such as the Rigveda.

Dayananda held that the Vedas taught one God and that much of later Hinduism was error. The Samaj rejected idol worship, caste by birth, child marriage and costly rituals, and backed the education of women and remarriage of widows. Dayananda set out his views in his book Satyarth Prakash, published the same year.

It differed from the Brahmo Samaj in Bengal. Where the Brahmos leaned on reason and Western ideas, the Arya Samaj claimed its authority from the Vedas alone and spoke sharply against Christianity and Islam.

Its strongest base was the Punjab. It built a network of schools and colleges, the first Dayanand Anglo Vedic college opening at Lahore in 1886, and ran a campaign of shuddhi, bringing converts back into Hinduism. Nationalists such as Lala Lajpat Rai came from its ranks. Its blend of reform and Hindu pride fed later Hindu nationalism.
sum: The Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in Bombay in 1875 by the monk Dayananda Saraswati. Its call was a return to the Vedas, the oldest Hindu scriptures, such as the Rigveda.
